import { expect, test } from 'bun:test';
import { denyListed } from './deny.ts';

const cwd = '/work/repo';
const hit = (line: string) => denyListed(line.split(' '), cwd)?.name;

test('force-push in all its forms', () => {
  for (const line of ['git push --force origin main', 'git push -f', 'git push -fu origin x', 'git push --force-with-lease', 'git push --force-with-lease=main:abc', 'git push origin +main', 'git push origin :old', 'git push origin --delete old', 'git push -d origin old', 'git push --mirror', 'git push --prune origin', '/usr/bin/git push -f', 'git -C sub push -f', 'git -c user.name=x push --force', 'git --git-dir .git push -f'])
    expect([line, hit(line)]).toEqual([line, 'force-push']);
});

test('ordinary pushes and other git commands pass', () => {
  for (const line of ['git push origin feature', 'git push -u origin feature', 'git push --tags', 'git status', 'git -C f push', 'git log --format=+x', 'git commit -m fix', 'git fetch --prune'])
    expect([line, hit(line)]).toEqual([line, undefined]);
});

test('reset --hard and clean -f', () => {
  expect(hit('git reset --hard HEAD~1')).toBe('reset-hard');
  expect(hit('git reset --soft HEAD~1')).toBeUndefined();
  for (const line of ['git clean -f', 'git clean -fdx', 'git clean -d --force', 'git clean -fn']) expect([line, hit(line)]).toEqual([line, 'clean-force']);
  for (const line of ['git clean -n', 'git clean -f -n', 'git clean -f --dry-run', 'git clean -d']) expect([line, hit(line)]).toEqual([line, undefined]);
});

test('rm -r outside the working directory', () => {
  for (const line of ['rm -rf /', 'rm -rf ~', 'rm -r ../other', 'rm -rf .', 'rm -rf /work/repo', 'rm -R /etc', 'rm --recursive /tmp/x', 'rm -rf $DIR', 'rm -rf ~bob/x', 'rm -rf', 'rm -fr src /etc'])
    expect([line, hit(line)]).toEqual([line, 'rm-outside']);
});

test('rm inside the working directory, or not recursive, passes', () => {
  for (const line of ['rm -rf node_modules dist', 'rm -rf ./*', 'rm -rf *', 'rm -r src/old', 'rm /tmp/x.txt', 'rm -f ../a.txt', 'rm -rf /work/repo/build', '/bin/rm -rf build'])
    expect([line, hit(line)]).toEqual([line, undefined]);
});

test('words after -- are targets', () => {
  expect(hit('rm -rf -- -weird')).toBeUndefined();
  expect(denyListed(['rm', '-rf', '--', '/etc'], cwd)?.name).toBe('rm-outside');
  expect(denyListed(['rm', '--', '-r', '/etc'], cwd)).toBeUndefined(); // -r after -- is a file name, so not recursive
});

test('find -delete and -exec', () => {
  for (const line of ['find / -name x -delete', 'find .. -exec rm {} ;', 'find $HOME -delete', 'find src /var -delete'])
    expect([line, hit(line)]).toEqual([line, 'rm-outside']);
  for (const line of ['find . -name *.tmp -delete', 'find -delete', 'find src -execdir touch {} ;', 'find / -name x'])
    expect([line, hit(line)]).toEqual([line, undefined]);
});

test('empty argv and other commands', () => {
  expect(denyListed([], cwd)).toBeUndefined();
  expect(hit('ls -la')).toBeUndefined();
});

import { expect, test } from 'bun:test';
import { denyListed } from './deny.ts';

const cwd = '/work/repo';
const hit = (line: string) => denyListed(line.split(' '), cwd)?.name;

test('force-push in all its forms', () => {
  for (const line of ['git push --force origin main', 'git push -f', 'git push -fu origin x', 'git push --force-with-lease', 'git push --force-with-lease=main:abc', 'git push origin +main', 'git push origin :old', 'git push origin --delete old', 'git push -d origin old', 'git push --mirror', 'git push --prune origin', '/usr/bin/git push -f', 'git -C sub push -f', 'git -c user.name=x push --force', 'git --git-dir .git push -f'])
    expect([line, hit(line)]).toEqual([line, 'force-push']);
});

test('ordinary pushes and other git commands pass', () => {
  for (const line of ['git push origin feature', 'git push -u origin feature', 'git push --tags', 'git status', 'git -C f push', 'git log --format=+x', 'git commit -m fix', 'git fetch --prune'])
    expect([line, hit(line)]).toEqual([line, undefined]);
});

test('reset --hard and clean -f', () => {
  expect(hit('git reset --hard HEAD~1')).toBe('reset-hard');
  expect(hit('git reset --soft HEAD~1')).toBeUndefined();
  for (const line of ['git clean -f', 'git clean -fdx', 'git clean -d --force', 'git clean -fn']) expect([line, hit(line)]).toEqual([line, 'clean-force']);
  for (const line of ['git clean -n', 'git clean -f -n', 'git clean -f --dry-run', 'git clean -d']) expect([line, hit(line)]).toEqual([line, undefined]);
});

test('rm -r outside the working directory', () => {
  for (const line of ['rm -rf /', 'rm -rf ~', 'rm -r ../other', 'rm -rf .', 'rm -rf /work/repo', 'rm -R /etc', 'rm --recursive /tmp/x', 'rm -rf $DIR', 'rm -rf ~bob/x', 'rm -rf', 'rm -fr src /etc'])
    expect([line, hit(line)]).toEqual([line, 'rm-outside']);
});

test('rm inside the working directory, or not recursive, passes', () => {
  for (const line of ['rm -rf node_modules dist', 'rm -rf ./*', 'rm -rf *', 'rm -r src/old', 'rm /tmp/x.txt', 'rm -f ../a.txt', 'rm -rf /work/repo/build', '/bin/rm -rf build'])
    expect([line, hit(line)]).toEqual([line, undefined]);
});

test('words after -- are targets', () => {

import { describe, expect, test } from 'bun:test';
import { applyEdit } from './edit.ts';

const SRC = 'function f() {\n    if (a) {\n        return 1;  \n    }\n}\n';
const ok = (r: ReturnType<typeof applyEdit>) => {
  if ('error' in r) throw new Error(r.error);
  return r;
};

describe('exact', () => {
  test('replaces one match and reports its lines', () => {
    const r = ok(applyEdit(SRC, { old_text: 'return 1;', new_text: 'return 2;' }));
    expect(r.applied).toEqual({ from: 3, to: 3, tier: 'exact', count: 1 });
    expect(r.content).toBe('function f() {\n    if (a) {\n        return 2;  \n    }\n}\n');
  });
  test('multi-line exact match spans its lines', () => {
    const r = ok(applyEdit('a\nb\nc\nd\n', { old_text: 'b\nc', new_text: 'B\nC\nX' }));
    expect(r.applied).toEqual({ from: 2, to: 3, tier: 'exact', count: 1 });
    expect(r.content).toBe('a\nB\nC\nX\nd\n');
  });
  test('ambiguous without replace_all', () => {
    const r = applyEdit('x\ny\nx\n', { old_text: 'x', new_text: 'z' });
    expect('error' in r && r.error).toContain('matches 2 places');
    expect('error' in r && r.error).toContain('line 1');
  });
  test('replace_all replaces every occurrence', () => {
    const r = ok(applyEdit('x\ny\nx\n', { old_text: 'x', new_text: 'z', replace_all: true }));
    expect(r.content).toBe('z\ny\nz\n');
    expect(r.applied.count).toBe(2);
    expect(r.applied.tier).toBe('exact');
  });
});

describe('trailing-space', () => {
  test('matches lines whose trailing spaces differ', () => {
    const r = ok(applyEdit(SRC, { old_text: '    if (a) {\n        return 1;\n    }', new_text: '    if (a) {\n        return 3;\n    }' }));
    expect(r.applied).toEqual({ from: 2, to: 4, tier: 'trailing-space', count: 1 });
    expect(r.content).toBe('function f() {\n    if (a) {\n        return 3;\n    }\n}\n');
  });
  test('a trailing newline on old_text and new_text is ignored', () => {
    const r = ok(applyEdit('a  \nb\n', { old_text: 'a\n', new_text: 'A\n' }));
    expect(r.content).toBe('A\nb\n');
  });
  test('two windows match: error with their lines', () => {
    const r = applyEdit('a \nb\na  \nb\n', { old_text: 'a\nb', new_text: 'c' });
    expect('error' in r && r.error).toContain('matches 2 places');
    expect('error' in r && r.error).toContain('1, 3');
  });
});

describe('indentation', () => {
  test('re-indents new_text to the file', () => {
    const r = ok(applyEdit(SRC, { old_text: 'if (a) {\n    return 1;\n}', new_text: 'if (b) {\n    return 1;\n}' }));
    expect(r.applied).toEqual({ from: 2, to: 4, tier: 'indentation', count: 1 });
    expect(r.content).toBe('function f() {\n    if (b) {\n        return 1;\n    }\n}\n');
  });
  test('tabs in the file, spaces in old_text', () => {
    const r = ok(applyEdit('if x:\n\tdo()\n\tdone()\n', { old_text: '  do()\n  done()', new_text: '  do()\n  log()\n  done()' }));
    expect(r.content).toBe('if x:\n\tdo()\n\tlog()\n\tdone()\n');
  });
  test('blank lines stay blank and empty new_text deletes', () => {
    const r = ok(applyEdit('a\n  b\n  c\nd\n', { old_text: 'b\nc', new_text: '' }));
    expect(r.content).toBe('a\nd\n');
    const r2 = ok(applyEdit('a\n  b\n  e\nd\n', { old_text: 'b\ne', new_text: 'b\n\nc' }));
    expect(r2.content).toBe('a\n  b\n\n  c\nd\n');
  });
});

describe('errors', () => {
  test('empty old_text and no-op edits', () => {
    expect(applyEdit(SRC, { old_text: '', new_text: 'x' })).toEqual({ error: expect.stringContaining('use write') });
    expect(applyEdit(SRC, { old_text: 'f()', new_text: 'f()' })).toEqual({ error: expect.stringContaining('same') });
  });
  test('not found points at where the first line appears', () => {
    const r = applyEdit(SRC, { old_text: 'if (a) {\n  return 9;', new_text: '' });
    expect('error' in r && r.error).toContain('not found');
    expect('error' in r && r.error).toContain('first line appears at line 2');
  });
  test('not found without a pointer when the first line is nowhere', () => {
    const r = applyEdit(SRC, { old_text: 'nothing like this', new_text: 'x' });
    expect('error' in r && r.error).toContain('not found');
    expect('error' in r && r.error).not.toContain('appears');
  });
});

// A slice of a coding agent's session log. Events are in order; `request` starts a new model call.
export type SessionEvent =

  | { kind: 'snapshot'; callId?: string; changed: string[] }
  | { kind: 'text'; text: string };

// `at` is the index of the tool_result event in the log.
export type LedgerEntry =
  | { kind: 'write'; at: number; tool: string; path?: string; command?: string }
  | { kind: 'check'; at: number; command: string; exitCode: number };

export type Evidence = { changed: string[]; checks: { command: string; exitCode: number }[]; unverified: string[] };

// Commands that only read. Given; do not change.

  return /^(ls|cat|head|tail|grep|rg|find|wc|pwd|echo|git (status|diff|log|show))(\s|$)/.test(command.trim()) && !/[>|;&]/.test(command);

import { resolve } from 'node:path';

// A slice of a coding agent's session log. Events are in order; `request` starts a new model call.
export type SessionEvent =
  | { kind: 'request' }
  | { kind: 'tool_intent'; callId: string; tool: string; input: Record<string, unknown> }
  | { kind: 'tool_result'; callId: string; status: 'completed' | 'failed' | 'denied' | 'not_started'; output: { isError: boolean; exitCode?: number } }
  | { kind: 'snapshot'; callId?: string; changed: string[] }
  | { kind: 'text'; text: string };

// `at` is the index of the tool_result event in the log.
export type LedgerEntry =
  | { kind: 'write'; at: number; tool: string; path?: string; command?: string }
  | { kind: 'check'; at: number; command: string; exitCode: number };

export type Evidence = { changed: string[]; checks: { command: string; exitCode: number }[]; unverified: string[] };

// Commands that only read. Given; do not change.
export function isReadOnly(command: string): boolean {
  return /^(ls|cat|head|tail|grep|rg|find|wc|pwd|echo|git (status|diff|log|show))(\s|$)/.test(command.trim()) && !/[>|;&]/.test(command);
}

// Returns the declared check (as written in `checks`) that a bash command runs, or undefined.
// The whole command must be the check, after trimming and collapsing whitespace on both, and dropping a trailing
// ` 2>&1` from both. A pipe or a chain would hide the check's exit code, so `bun test | tail` does not count.
// One exception: a leading `cd <dir> && ` is removed when <dir> (quotes stripped) resolves to `cwd`.
export function matchCheck(command: string, checks: string[], cwd?: string): string | undefined {
  throw new Error('not implemented');
}

// Walks the log and returns one entry per thing that happened, in log order.
// - Only tool_results whose call has a tool_intent since the last `request` count; denied and not_started
//   results never count.
// - A bash call (input.command) whose command matches a check is a check entry: exitCode from the output,
//   or 1 when it has none and isError is set, else 0. A check never counts as a write.
// - Otherwise, when a snapshot event anywhere in the log names this callId, one write entry per changed path
//   (none when the list is empty).
// - Otherwise an edit or write call that completed is a write entry with path = input.path.
// - Otherwise a bash call whose command is not read-only is a write entry with command set (no path).
export function ledgerEntries(events: SessionEvent[], checks: string[], cwd?: string): LedgerEntry[] {
  throw new Error('not implemented');
}

// changed: every write's label (path, or `bash: <command>`), first seen first, no duplicates.
// checks: every check entry, in order, as { command, exitCode }.
// unverified: labels of writes after the last passing check (all of them when no check passed), deduped.
export function evidence(entries: LedgerEntry[]): Evidence {
  throw new Error('not implemented');
}

// The done gate. With no declared checks, or no writes, it is satisfied. Otherwise a check with exit code 0
// must come after the last write.
export function verified(entries: LedgerEntry[], checks: string[]): boolean {
  throw new Error('not implemented');
}

// bash words that name them, so their contents never reach a model provider.
export function secretPaths(cediaHome: string, home = homedir()): string[] {
  return ['.ssh', '.aws', '.gnupg', '.config/gh', '.netrc', '.docker/config.json', '.git-credentials', '.npmrc', '.pypirc', '.kube/config']

import { expect, test } from 'bun:test';
import { simpleCommands } from './shell.ts';

test('chains, pipes and background jobs', () => {
  expect(simpleCommands('a x && b | c; d & e || f')).toEqual([['a', 'x'], ['b'], ['c'], ['d'], ['e'], ['f']]);
  expect(simpleCommands('a\nb')).toEqual([['a'], ['b']]);
});

test('substitutions and subshells are commands of their own', () => {
  expect(simpleCommands('echo $(rm -rf /) `id`')).toEqual([['echo'], ['rm', '-rf', '/'], ['id']]);
  expect(simpleCommands('(cd x && make)')).toEqual([['cd', 'x'], ['make']]);
});

test('quotes and escapes', () => {
  expect(simpleCommands(`grep "a b" 'c;d' e\\ f`)).toEqual([['grep', 'a b', 'c;d', 'e f']]);
  expect(simpleCommands(`echo "say \\"hi\\"" ''`)).toEqual([['echo', 'say "hi"', '']]);
  expect(simpleCommands(`echo 'a\\b'`)).toEqual([['echo', 'a\\b']]);
  expect(simpleCommands('echo "open')).toBeNull();
  expect(simpleCommands("echo 'open")).toBeNull();
});

test('redirections are not commands and leave argv', () => {
  expect(simpleCommands('ls 2>&1 > out.txt | grep "a b"')).toEqual([['ls'], ['grep', 'a b']]);
  expect(simpleCommands('cmd >out.txt 2>/dev/null arg')).toEqual([['cmd', 'arg']]);
  expect(simpleCommands('cmd &> log arg')).toEqual([['cmd', 'arg']]);
  expect(simpleCommands('sort < in.txt')).toEqual([['sort']]);
});

test('assignments, keywords and wrappers are unwrapped', () => {
  expect(simpleCommands('sudo -E env A=1 git push -f')).toEqual([['git', 'push', '-f']]);
  expect(simpleCommands('FOO=1 BAR=2 npm publish')).toEqual([['npm', 'publish']]);
  expect(simpleCommands('if true; then rm -r /tmp/x; fi')).toEqual([['true'], ['rm', '-r', '/tmp/x']]);
  expect(simpleCommands('{ rm -rf /; }')).toEqual([['rm', '-rf', '/']]);
  expect(simpleCommands('find . | xargs -0 rm -rf')).toEqual([['find', '.'], ['rm', '-rf']]);
  expect(simpleCommands('nohup time nice -n 5 make')).toEqual([['make']]);
  expect(simpleCommands('timeout -k 2 10s sudo -u root -- git push -f')).toEqual([['git', 'push', '-f']]);
});

test('bash -c and eval are unpacked', () => {
  expect(simpleCommands(`bash -c "git reset --hard && ls"`)).toEqual([['git', 'reset', '--hard'], ['ls']]);
  expect(simpleCommands(`sh -c 'rm -fr /etc'`)).toEqual([['rm', '-fr', '/etc']]);
  expect(simpleCommands('eval git push --force')).toEqual([['git', 'push', '--force']]);
  expect(simpleCommands(`sudo bash -c "cd / && rm -rf *"`)).toEqual([['cd', '/'], ['rm', '-rf', '*']]);
});

test('empty input and empty commands', () => {
  expect(simpleCommands('')).toEqual([]);
  expect(simpleCommands(' ; ; ')).toEqual([]);
  expect(simpleCommands('a;;b')).toEqual([['a'], ['b']]);
});

import { expect, test } from 'bun:test';
import { readSse, streamFromString, type SseMessage } from './sse.ts';

async function all(text: string, chunk = 7): Promise<SseMessage[]> {
  const out: SseMessage[] = [];
  for await (const m of readSse(streamFromString(text, chunk))) out.push(m);
  return out;
}

test('events and data, at every chunk size', async () => {
  const text = 'event: message_start\ndata: {"a":1}\n\nevent: delta\ndata: {"b":2}\n\n';
  for (const chunk of [1, 2, 3, 5, 64])
    expect(await all(text, chunk)).toEqual([
      { event: 'message_start', data: '{"a":1}' },
      { event: 'delta', data: '{"b":2}' },
    ]);
});

test('CRLF line endings, split between chunks too', async () => {
  for (const chunk of [1, 4, 100]) expect(await all('event: x\r\ndata: 1\r\n\r\ndata: 2\r\n\r\n', chunk)).toEqual([{ event: 'x', data: '1' }, { data: '2' }]);
});

test('multi-line data, comments and unknown fields', async () => {
  expect(await all(': keep-alive\ndata: a\nid: 7\ndata: b\nretry: 100\n\n:\n\n')).toEqual([{ data: 'a\nb' }]);
});

test('only the first space after the colon is dropped; a bare field is empty', async () => {
  expect(await all('data:no-space\n\ndata:   two spaces\n\ndata\n\n')).toEqual([{ data: 'no-space' }, { data: '  two spaces' }, { data: '' }]);
});

test('event resets after each message, and an event without data is dropped', async () => {
  expect(await all('event: ping\n\ndata: plain\n\nevent: a\ndata: x\n\ndata: y\n\n')).toEqual([{ data: 'plain' }, { event: 'a', data: 'x' }, { data: 'y' }]);
});

test('multi-byte characters split across chunks', async () => {
  for (const chunk of [1, 2, 3]) expect(await all('data: สวัสดี 🙂\n\n', chunk)).toEqual([{ data: 'สวัสดี 🙂' }]);
});

test('a body that ends without a blank line still yields its data', async () => {
  expect(await all('data: one\n\ndata: [DONE]')).toEqual([{ data: 'one' }, { data: '[DONE]' }]);
  expect(await all('data: last\n')).toEqual([{ data: 'last' }]);
  expect(await all('')).toEqual([]);
});

test('messages are yielded as they arrive, before the body ends', async () => {
  let release!: () => void;
  const gate = new Promise<void>((r) => (release = r));
  const enc = new TextEncoder();
  let step = 0;
  const body = new ReadableStream<Uint8Array>({
    async pull(c) {
      if (step === 0) c.enqueue(enc.encode('data: first\n\n'));
      else if (step === 1) {
        await gate;
        c.enqueue(enc.encode('data: second\n\n'));
      } else c.close();
      step++;
    },
  });
  const it = readSse(body);
  const first = await Promise.race([it.next(), new Promise((r) => setTimeout(() => r('timeout'), 500))]);
  expect(first).toEqual({ value: { data: 'first' }, done: false });
  release();
  expect((await it.next()).value).toEqual({ data: 'second' });
  expect((await it.next()).done).toBe(true);
});

import { expect, test } from 'bun:test';
import { readSse, streamFromString, type SseMessage } from './sse.ts';

async function all(text: string, chunk = 7): Promise<SseMessage[]> {
  const out: SseMessage[] = [];
  for await (const m of readSse(streamFromString(text, chunk))) out.push(m);
  return out;
}

test('events and data, at every chunk size', async () => {
  const text = 'event: message_start\ndata: {"a":1}\n\nevent: delta\ndata: {"b":2}\n\n';
  for (const chunk of [1, 2, 3, 5, 64])
    expect(await all(text, chunk)).toEqual([
      { event: 'message_start', data: '{"a":1}' },
      { event: 'delta', data: '{"b":2}' },
    ]);
});

test('CRLF line endings, split between chunks too', async () => {
  for (const chunk of [1, 4, 100]) expect(await all('event: x\r\ndata: 1\r\n\r\ndata: 2\r\n\r\n', chunk)).toEqual([{ event: 'x', data: '1' }, { data: '2' }]);
});

test('multi-line data, comments and unknown fields', async () => {
  expect(await all(': keep-alive\ndata: a\nid: 7\ndata: b\nretry: 100\n\n:\n\n')).toEqual([{ data: 'a\nb' }]);
});

test('only the first space after the colon is dropped; a bare field is empty', async () => {
  expect(await all('data:no-space\n\ndata:   two spaces\n\ndata\n\n')).toEqual([{ data: 'no-space' }, { data: '  two spaces' }, { data: '' }]);
});

test('event resets after each message, and an event without data is dropped', async () => {
  expect(await all('event: ping\n\ndata: plain\n\nevent: a\ndata: x\n\ndata: y\n\n')).toEqual([{ data: 'plain' }, { event: 'a', data: 'x' }, { data: 'y' }]);
});

test('multi-byte characters split across chunks', async () => {
  for (const chunk of [1, 2, 3]) expect(await all('data: สวัสดี 🙂\n\n', chunk)).toEqual([{ data: 'สวัสดี 🙂' }]);
});

test('a body that ends without a blank line still yields its data', async () => {
  expect(await all('data: one\n\ndata: [DONE]')).toEqual([{ data: 'one' }, { data: '[DONE]' }]);
  expect(await all('data: last\n')).toEqual([{ data: 'last' }]);
  expect(await all('')).toEqual([]);
});

test('messages are yielded as they arrive, before the body ends', async () => {
  let release!: () => void;
  const gate = new Promise<void>((r) => (release = r));
  const enc = new TextEncoder();
  let step = 0;
  const body = new ReadableStream<Uint8Array>({
    async pull(c) {
      if (step === 0) c.enqueue(enc.encode('data: first\n\n'));
      else if (step === 1) {
        await gate;
        c.enqueue(enc.encode('data: second\n\n'));
      } else c.close();
      step++;
    },
  });
  const it = readSse(body);
  const first = await Promise.race([it.next(), new Promise((r) => setTimeout(() => r('timeout'), 500))]);
  expect(first).toEqual({ value: { data: 'first' }, done: false });
  release();
  expect((await it.next()).value).toEqual({ data: 'second' });
  expect((await it.next()).done).toBe(true);
});

// An in-memory table store with two APIs: the old callback one and db.promises. They share the same data.
export type Row = { id: string; [field: string]: unknown };
type Cb<T> = (err: Error | null, value?: T) => void;

let tables = new Map<string, Map<string, Row>>();

export function reset(seed: Record<string, Row[]> = {}): void {
  tables = new Map(Object.entries(seed).map(([t, rows]) => [t, new Map(rows.map((r) => [r.id, { ...r }]))]));
}

const table = (name: string) => {
  let t = tables.get(name);
  if (!t) tables.set(name, (t = new Map()));
  return t;
};

const get = (t: string, id: string): Row | undefined => {
  const r = table(t).get(id);
  return r && { ...r };
};
const put = (t: string, row: Row): Row => {
  table(t).set(row.id, { ...row });
  return { ...row };
};
const remove = (t: string, id: string): boolean => table(t).delete(id);
const query = (t: string, where: (r: Row) => boolean): Row[] => [...table(t).values()].filter(where).map((r) => ({ ...r }));

const later = <T>(f: () => T, cb: Cb<T>) =>
  queueMicrotask(() => {
    try {
      cb(null, f());
    } catch (e) {
      cb(e as Error);
    }
  });

export const db = {
  get: (t: string, id: string, cb: Cb<Row | undefined>) => later(() => get(t, id), cb),
  put: (t: string, row: Row, cb: Cb<Row>) => later(() => put(t, row), cb),
  remove: (t: string, id: string, cb: Cb<boolean>) => later(() => remove(t, id), cb),
  query: (t: string, where: (r: Row) => boolean, cb: Cb<Row[]>) => later(() => query(t, where), cb),
  promises: {
    get: async (t: string, id: string) => get(t, id),
    put: async (t: string, row: Row) => put(t, row),
    remove: async (t: string, id: string) => remove(t, id),
    query: async (t: string, where: (r: Row) => boolean) => query(t, where),
  },
};
export class HttpError extends Error {
  constructor(
    readonly status: number,
    message: string,
  ) {
    super(message);
  }

export function renameUser(req: { id: string; name: string }, done: (err: Error | null, res?: Row) => void): void {
  db.get('users', req.id, (err, user) => {
    if (err) return done(err);
    if (!user) return done(new HttpError(404, `no user ${req.id}`));
    const name = req.name.trim();
    if (!name) return done(new HttpError(400, 'name is required'));
    if (name === user.name) return done(null, user);
    db.put('users', { ...user, name }, done);
  });
}

import { db, type Row } from '../../db.ts';
import { HttpError } from '../../errors.ts';

// Cancels an open order and puts its units back in stock.
export function cancelOrder(req: { id: string }, done: (err: Error | null, res?: Row) => void): void {
  db.get('orders', req.id, (err, order) => {
    if (err) return done(err);
    if (!order) return done(new HttpError(404, `no order ${req.id}`));
    if (order.status !== 'open') return done(new HttpError(409, `order ${req.id} is ${order.status}`));
    db.get('stock', order.sku as string, (err2, stock) => {
      if (err2) return done(err2);
      const units = ((stock?.units as number | undefined) ?? 0) + (order.quantity as number);
      db.put('stock', { id: order.sku as string, units }, (err3) => {
        if (err3) return done(err3);
        db.put('orders', { ...order, status: 'cancelled' }, done);
      });
    });
  });
}

// Moves units of one sku to another sku's count (a repack). Both rows are written, source first.
export function transferStock(req: { from: string; to: string; units: number }, done: (err: Error | null, res?: { from: Row; to: Row }) => void): void {
  if (req.from === req.to) return done(new HttpError(400, 'from and to are the same'));
  db.get('stock', req.from, (err, a) => {
    if (err) return done(err);
    const have = (a?.units as number | undefined) ?? 0;
    if (have < req.units) return done(new HttpError(409, `only ${have} ${req.from} left`));
    db.get('stock', req.to, (err2, b) => {
      if (err2) return done(err2);
      db.put('stock', { id: req.from, units: have - req.units }, (err3, from) => {
        if (err3) return done(err3);
        db.put('stock', { id: req.to, units: ((b?.units as number | undefined) ?? 0) + req.units }, (err4, to) => {
          if (err4) return done(err4);
          done(null, { from: from!, to: to! });
        });
      });
    });
  });
}

import { db, type Row } from '../../db.ts';
import { HttpError } from '../../errors.ts';

// Adds delta units (negative to remove); stock never goes below zero.
export function adjustStock(req: { sku: string; delta: number }, done: (err: Error | null, res?: Row) => void): void {
  if (!Number.isInteger(req.delta) || req.delta === 0) return done(new HttpError(400, 'delta must be a non-zero integer'));
  db.get('stock', req.sku, (err, stock) => {
    if (err) return done(err);
    const units = ((stock?.units as number | undefined) ?? 0) + req.delta;
    if (units < 0) return done(new HttpError(409, `stock of ${req.sku} would be ${units}`));
    db.put('stock', { id: req.sku, units }, done);
  });
}

import { db, type Row } from '../../db.ts';
import { HttpError } from '../../errors.ts';

// Counts per order status and total units ordered, over all orders of active users.
export function summary(_req: {}, done: (err: Error | null, res?: { byStatus: Record<string, number>; units: number }) => void): void {
  db.query('users', (u) => u.active !== false, (err, users) => {
    if (err) return done(err);
    const active = new Set((users ?? []).map((u) => u.id));
    db.query('orders', (o) => active.has(o.user as string), (err2, orders) => {
      if (err2) return done(err2);
      const byStatus: Record<string, number> = {};
      let units = 0;
      for (const o of orders ?? []) {
        byStatus[o.status as string] = (byStatus[o.status as string] ?? 0) + 1;
        units += o.quantity as number;
      }
      done(null, { byStatus, units });
    });
  });
}

// An in-memory table store with two APIs: the old callback one and db.promises. They share the same data.
export type Row = { id: string; [field: string]: unknown };
type Cb<T> = (err: Error | null, value?: T) => void;

let tables = new Map<string, Map<string, Row>>();

export function reset(seed: Record<string, Row[]> = {}): void {
  tables = new Map(Object.entries(seed).map(([t, rows]) => [t, new Map(rows.map((r) => [r.id, { ...r }]))]));
}

const table = (name: string) => {
  let t = tables.get(name);
  if (!t) tables.set(name, (t = new Map()));
  return t;
};

const get = (t: string, id: string): Row | undefined => {
  const r = table(t).get(id);
  return r && { ...r };
};
const put = (t: string, row: Row): Row => {
  table(t).set(row.id, { ...row });
  return { ...row };
};
const remove = (t: string, id: string): boolean => table(t).delete(id);
const query = (t: string, where: (r: Row) => boolean): Row[] => [...table(t).values()].filter(where).map((r) => ({ ...r }));

const later = <T>(f: () => T, cb: Cb<T>) =>
  queueMicrotask(() => {
    try {
      cb(null, f());
    } catch (e) {
      cb(e as Error);
    }
  });

export const db = {
  get: (t: string, id: string, cb: Cb<Row | undefined>) => later(() => get(t, id), cb),
  put: (t: string, row: Row, cb: Cb<Row>) => later(() => put(t, row), cb),
  remove: (t: string, id: string, cb: Cb<boolean>) => later(() => remove(t, id), cb),
  query: (t: string, where: (r: Row) => boolean, cb: Cb<Row[]>) => later(() => query(t, where), cb),
  promises: {
    get: async (t: string, id: string) => get(t, id),
    put: async (t: string, row: Row) => put(t, row),
    remove: async (t: string, id: string) => remove(t, id),
    query: async (t: string, where: (r: Row) => boolean) => query(t, where),
  },
};
export class HttpError extends Error {
  constructor(
    readonly status: number,
    message: string,
  ) {
    super(message);
  }
}

import { db, type Row } from '../../db.ts';
import { HttpError } from '../../errors.ts';

export function renameUser(req: { id: string; name: string }, done: (err: Error | null, res?: Row) => void): void {
  db.get('users', req.id, (err, user) => {
    if (err) return done(err);
    if (!user) return done(new HttpError(404, `no user ${req.id}`));
    const name = req.name.trim();
    if (!name) return done(new HttpError(400, 'name is required'));
    if (name === user.name) return done(null, user);
    db.put('users', { ...user, name }, done);
  });
}

  });
  test('deactivateUser cancels open orders', async () => {
    expect(await deactivateUser({ id: 'u1' })).toEqual({ cancelled: 2 });
    expect(await db.promises.get('users', 'u1')).toMatchObject({ active: false });
    expect((await db.promises.query('orders', (o) => o.user === 'u1')).map((o) => o.status).sort()).toEqual(['cancelled', 'cancelled', 'shipped']);
    await fails(deactivateUser({ id: 'zz' }), 404, 'no user zz');
  });
});

describe('orders', () => {
  test('createOrder takes stock', async () => {
    expect(await createOrder({ id: 'o9', user: 'u2', sku: 'MUG', quantity: 4 })).toMatchObject({ status: 'open', quantity: 4 });
    expect(await db.promises.get('stock', 'MUG')).toMatchObject({ units: 6 });
    await fails(createOrder({ id: 'o10', user: 'u2', sku: 'TEE', quantity: 3 }), 409, 'only 2 TEE left');
    await fails(createOrder({ id: 'o11', user: 'u3', sku: 'MUG', quantity: 1 }), 404, 'no user u3');
    await fails(createOrder({ id: 'o12', user: 'u2', sku: 'MUG', quantity: 0 }), 400, 'quantity must be a positive integer');
    expect(await db.promises.get('orders', 'o10')).toBeUndefined();
  });
  test('listOrders', async () => {
    expect((await listOrders({ user: 'u1' })).map((o) => o.id)).toEqual(['o3', 'o2', 'o1']);
    expect((await listOrders({ user: 'u1', status: 'open' })).map((o) => o.id)).toEqual(['o3', 'o1']);
    expect(await listOrders({ user: 'nobody' })).toEqual([]);
  });
  test('cancelOrder returns units', async () => {
    expect(await cancelOrder({ id: 'o3' })).toMatchObject({ status: 'cancelled' });
    expect(await db.promises.get('stock', 'MUG')).toMatchObject({ units: 12 });
    await fails(cancelOrder({ id: 'o2' }), 409, 'order o2 is shipped');
    await fails(cancelOrder({ id: 'o3' }), 409, 'order o3 is cancelled');
    await fails(cancelOrder({ id: 'zz' }), 404, 'no order zz');
  });
});

describe('stock and reports', () => {
  test('adjustStock', async () => {
    expect(await adjustStock({ sku: 'TEE', delta: 3 })).toEqual({ id: 'TEE', units: 5 });
    expect(await adjustStock({ sku: 'NEW', delta: 1 })).toEqual({ id: 'NEW', units: 1 });
    await fails(adjustStock({ sku: 'TEE', delta: -9 }), 409, 'stock of TEE would be -4');
    await fails(adjustStock({ sku: 'TEE', delta: 0 }), 400, 'delta must be a non-zero integer');
  });
  test('transferStock', async () => {
    expect(await transferStock({ from: 'MUG', to: 'TEE', units: 4 })).toEqual({ from: { id: 'MUG', units: 6 }, to: { id: 'TEE', units: 6 } });
    await fails(transferStock({ from: 'TEE', to: 'MUG', units: 7 }), 409, 'only 6 TEE left');
    await fails(transferStock({ from: 'MUG', to: 'MUG', units: 1 }), 400, 'from and to are the same');
  });
  test('summary leaves out inactive users', async () => {
    expect(await summary({})).toEqual({ byStatus: { open: 2, shipped: 1 }, units: 4 });
  });
});

test('no handler uses the callback API any more', () => {
  const files = (dir: string): string[] =>
    readdirSync(dir, { withFileTypes: true }).flatMap((e) => (e.isDirectory() ? files(join(dir, e.name)) : [join(dir, e.name)]));
  for (const f of files(join(import.meta.dir, '..', 'src', 'handlers'))) {
    const src = readFileSync(f, 'utf8');
    expect([f, /\bdone\b|\bdb\.(get|put|remove|query)\(/.test(src)]).toEqual([f, false]);
  }
});

# AGENTS.md

Guidance for coding agents working in this repository. `CLAUDE.md` points here.

## What this is

cedia is a personal coding harness written from scratch in TypeScript on Bun. `SPEC.md` holds every settled decision and the stage order; read it before changing scope.

## Commands

- `bun test`: all tests. One file: `bun test test/layers.test.ts`. One test: add `-t "<name>"`.
- `bun run typecheck`: `tsc --noEmit`.
- `bin/cedia -p "<prompt>" [-m <model>] [--output-format text|json|stream-json] [--permission read-only|workspace] [--allow <rule>] [--deny <rule>]`: headless run. Read-only unless `--permission workspace`. `--check <cmd>` declares a check for the done gate. `--sandbox auto|on|off` controls the OS sandbox for bash (Linux needs bubblewrap, socat, ripgrep).
- `bin/cedia lint-session <file.jsonl>...`: check a session log against the trust invariants. `-m faux` with `CEDIA_FAUX_SCRIPT=<steps.json>` runs offline.
- `bun scripts/cache-probe.ts --model <ref> [--turns 20] [--runs 3]`: measure prompt-cache hits on a real model and name every miss.
- `bun evals/run.ts --harness <name> [--model <ref>] [--runs 3] [--jobs 4] [--budget <usd>] [--only <ids>]`: run the eval tasks against a harness; `--estimate --model <ref> [--measured <results.jsonl>]` prices a run first. Binaries come from `CEDIA_EVAL_<NAME>_BIN` or PATH. Results go in `evals/results/`.

## How to work

Work the pstack poteto-mode way:

- Name the data shapes before writing logic.
- Prove it works: every done-criterion has a test or a command that reruns.
- Decide by experiment (prototype or eval) instead of asking when the question can be measured.
- Small commits, each one a unit that can be checked.

## Rules that are easy to get wrong

- `src/core` and `src/protocol` never import from `src/clients`. `test/layers.test.ts` enforces it.
- Model-visible means logged: anything that reaches the model is an event in the session log first.
- Keep the cached prefix byte-identical (see "Cache rules" in `SPEC.md`). Never edit message 0 mid-session.
- Every `tool_use` gets a `tool_result`, including denied and not-started calls.
- API keys only. Never add Claude.ai OAuth, Cursor login, or any request that impersonates another client.
- Never copy code or prompts from `anthropics/claude-code` (no license) or leaked sources, and never port cedia-rs. Adapted Apache-2.0/MIT code needs a `NOTICE` entry.
- e2e tests use the faux provider and must work offline.

## Research

- `research/NOTES.md`: distilled findings with source paths.
- `research/mirror-docs.sh`: re-downloads official docs into `research/docs/` (gitignored). Grep there before searching the web.
</project_instructions>"}

const change = (path: string, added: string[], removed: string[] = [], deleted = false): FileChange => ({ path, added, removed, deleted });
const rules = (c: FileChange[]) => findSlop(c).map((f) => `${f.rule} ${f.path}`);

describe('findSlop', () => {
  test('tests deleted, weakened or skipped', () => {
    expect(rules([change('src/a.test.ts', [], [], true)])).toEqual(['test-deleted src/a.test.ts']);
    expect(rules([change('tests/test_x.py', ['    pass'], ['    assert x == 1', '    assert y == 2'])])).toEqual(['test-weakened tests/test_x.py']);
    expect(rules([change('a.test.ts', ["test.skip('x', () => {})"]), change('b_test.go', ['\tt.Skip("flaky")'])])).toEqual(['test-skipped a.test.ts', 'test-skipped b_test.go']);
    expect(rules([change('a.test.ts', ["  expect(f(2)).toBe(4);"], ["  expect(f(1)).toBe(2);"])])).toEqual([]); // rewritten, not weakened
    expect(rules([change('src/a.ts', [], [], true)])).toEqual([]); // deleting source is not test slop
  });

  test('silenced checks, swallowed errors, type escapes and stubs', () => {
    expect(
      rules([
        change('src/a.ts', ['// @ts-ignore', '/* eslint-disable */', 'try { f() } catch {}', 'const x = y as any;', "throw new Error('not implemented');"]),
        change('app.py', ['x = f()  # type: ignore', 'except Exception:  pass', 'raise NotImplementedError']),
      ]),
    ).toEqual([
      'suppression src/a.ts',
      'suppression src/a.ts',
      'swallowed-error src/a.ts',
      'type-escape src/a.ts',
      'stub src/a.ts',
      'suppression app.py',
      'swallowed-error app.py',
      'stub app.py',
    ]);
  });

  test('ordinary code is not flagged', () => {
    expect(
      rules([
        change('src/a.ts', ['try { f() } catch (e) { log(e); throw e; }', 'const company = "acme";', 'type Many = string[];', 'it.each(cases)("works", run);']),
        change('notes.md', ['as any reader knows, catch {} is bad']),
      ]),
    ).toEqual([]);
  });
});

    const quiet = await runPrompt({ log: off, provider: fauxProvider(steps()), model: FAUX_MODEL, tools: CORE_TOOLS, system: 's', cwd: cwd2, permission: { mode: 'workspace', allow: [], deny: [], unlock: ['slop-check'] } }, 'go');
    expect(quiet.subtype).toBe('success');
    expect(off.events.some((e) => e.kind === 'reminder')).toBe(false);
    expect(quiet.evidence?.flags).toBeUndefined();
  });

  test('detected checks remind once but never refuse', async () => {
    const cwd = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'cedia-soft-'));
    const script = [{ blocks: [toolUse('c1', 'write', { path: 'b.txt', content: 'x\n' })] }, { blocks: [text('done')] }, { blocks: [text('done')] }];
    const opts = { model: FAUX_MODEL, tools: CORE_TOOLS, system: 's', cwd, checks: ['bun test'], permission: { mode: 'workspace' as const, allow: [], deny: [] } };
    expect((await runPrompt({ ...opts, log: SessionLog.create(), provider: fauxProvider(script), softChecks: true }, 'go')).subtype).toBe('success');
    expect((await runPrompt({ ...opts, log: SessionLog.create(), provider: fauxProvider(script) }, 'go')).subtype).toBe('error_unverified_claim');
  });
});

test('detectChecks finds the repo test command', () => {
  const dir = (files: Record<string, string>) => {
    const d = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'cedia-detect-'));
    for (const [f, c] of Object.entries(files)) writeFileSync(join(d, f), c);
    return d;
  };
  expect(detectChecks(dir({ 'package.json': '{"scripts":{"test":"vitest run"}}', 'pnpm-lock.yaml': '' }))).toEqual(['pnpm test']);
  expect(detectChecks(dir({ 'package.json': '{"scripts":{"test":"bun test"}}', 'bun.lock': '' }))).toEqual(['bun run test']);
  expect(detectChecks(dir({ 'package.json': '{"scripts":{"test":"echo \\"Error: no test specified\\" && exit 1"}}' }))).toEqual([]);
  expect(detectChecks(dir({ 'Cargo.toml': '' }))).toEqual(['cargo test']);
  expect(detectChecks(dir({ 'go.mod': '' }))).toEqual(['go test ./...']);
  expect(detectChecks(dir({ Makefile: 'build:\n\tcc x.c\ntest:\n\t./run\n' }))).toEqual(['make test']);
  expect(detectChecks(dir({ 'README.md': '' }))).toEqual([]);
});

# AGENTS.md

Guidance for coding agents working in this repository. `CLAUDE.md` points here.

## What this is

cedia is a personal coding harness written from scratch in TypeScript on Bun. `SPEC.md` holds every settled decision and the stage order; read it before changing scope.

## Commands

- `bun test`: all tests. One file: `bun test test/layers.test.ts`. One test: add `-t "<name>"`.
- `bun run typecheck`: `tsc --noEmit`.
- `bin/cedia -p "<prompt>" [-m <model>] [--output-format text|json|stream-json] [--permission read-only|workspace] [--allow <rule>] [--deny <rule>]`: headless run. Read-only unless `--permission workspace`. `--check <cmd>` declares a check for the done gate. `--sandbox auto|on|off` controls the OS sandbox for bash (Linux needs bubblewrap, socat, ripgrep).
- `bin/cedia lint-session <file.jsonl>...`: check a session log against the trust invariants. `-m faux` with `CEDIA_FAUX_SCRIPT=<steps.json>` runs offline.
- `bun scripts/cache-probe.ts --model <ref> [--turns 20] [--runs 3]`: measure prompt-cache hits on a real model and name every miss.
- `bun evals/run.ts --harness <name> [--model <ref>] [--runs 3] [--jobs 4] [--budget <usd>] [--only <ids>]`: run the eval tasks against a harness; `--estimate --model <ref> [--measured <results.jsonl>]` prices a run first. Binaries come from `CEDIA_EVAL_<NAME>_BIN` or PATH. Results go in `evals/results/`.

## How to work

Work the pstack poteto-mode way:

- Name the data shapes before writing logic.
- Prove it works: every done-criterion has a test or a command that reruns.
- Decide by experiment (prototype or eval) instead of asking when the question can be measured.
- Small commits, each one a unit that can be checked.

## Rules that are easy to get wrong

- `src/core` and `src/protocol` never import from `src/clients`. `test/layers.test.ts` enforces it.
- Model-visible means logged: anything that reaches the model is an event in the session log first.
- Keep the cached prefix byte-identical (see "Cache rules" in `SPEC.md`). Never edit message 0 mid-session.
- Every `tool_use` gets a `tool_result`, including denied and not-started calls.
- API keys only. Never add Claude.ai OAuth, Cursor login, or any request that impersonates another client.
- Never copy code or prompts from `anthropics/claude-code` (no license) or leaked sources, and never port cedia-rs. Adapted Apache-2.0/MIT code needs a `NOTICE` entry.
- e2e tests use the faux provider and must work offline.

## Research

- `research/NOTES.md`: distilled findings with source paths.
- `research/mirror-docs.sh`: re-downloads official docs into `research/docs/` (gitignored). Grep there before searching the web.
</project_instructions>"}

# AGENTS.md

Guidance for coding agents working in this repository. `CLAUDE.md` points here.

## What this is

cedia is a personal coding harness written from scratch in TypeScript on Bun. `SPEC.md` holds every settled decision and the stage order; read it before changing scope. `docs/ROADMAP.md` says what comes next.

## Commands

- `bun test`: all tests. One file: `bun test test/layers.test.ts`. One test: add `-t "<name>"`.
- `bun run typecheck`: `tsc --noEmit`.
- `bin/cedia -p "<prompt>" [-m <model>] [--output-format text|json|stream-json] [--permission read-only|workspace] [--allow <rule>] [--deny <rule>]`: headless run. Read-only unless `--permission workspace`. `--check <cmd>` declares a check for the done gate. `--sandbox auto|on|off` controls the OS sandbox for bash (Linux needs bubblewrap, socat, ripgrep). `--fallback <ref|none>` names the model a run continues on when its quota runs out (default `deepseek` → `anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5`). `--plan <ref>` and `--review <ref>` add the plan and review roles (`claude-code[:<model>]` runs them in the user's own Claude Code); `roles` in `~/.cedia/settings.json` sets all three. `CEDIA_CLAUDE_BIN` points tests at a fake `claude`. Every run is a thread of the project: `--thread <id>` goes on with one, `--handoff-at <n|off>` sets when a long session hands off to a new one, `--spawn on|off` and `--swarm <ref>` control sub-threads.
- `bin/cedia threads [list [--all] | show <id> | send <id> <text> | archive <id>]`: the project's threads.
- `bin/cedia lint-session <file.jsonl>...`: check a session log against the trust invariants. `-m faux` with `CEDIA_FAUX_SCRIPT=<steps.json>` runs offline.
- `bun scripts/protocol-schema.ts` regenerates `src/protocol/protocol.schema.json` after a protocol type changes; `bun scripts/session-fixtures.ts` re-records `test/fixtures/sessions/` after the output of a run changes. `test/fixtures.test.ts` fails when either is stale.
- `bun scripts/cache-probe.ts --model <ref> [--turns 20] [--runs 3]`: measure prompt-cache hits on a real model and name every miss.
- `bun evals/run.ts --harness <name> [--model <ref>] [--runs 3] [--jobs 4] [--budget <usd>] [--only <ids>] [--cedia-arg=<flag>]`: run the eval tasks against a harness; `--estimate --model <ref> [--measured <results.jsonl>]` prices a run first. Binaries come from `CEDIA_EVAL_<NAME>_BIN` or PATH. Results go in `evals/results/`.
- `bun evals/gate.ts [--model <ref>] [--estimate] [--update-baseline]`: the regression gate. Runs `evals/gate/suite.json`, prints the expected cost first, compares with `evals/gate/baseline/` and exits 1 when a model got worse. `--compare <results.jsonl>` re-scores a result file for free. Run it before merging a change to a prompt, default, the loop, a tool or the trust layer (`evals/gate/README.md`).

## How to work

Work the pstack poteto-mode way:

- Name the data shapes before writing logic.
- Prove it works: every done-criterion has a test or a command that reruns.
- Decide by experiment (prototype or eval) instead of asking when the question can be measured.
- Small commits, each one a unit that can be checked.

## Rules that are easy to get wrong

- `src/core` and `src/protocol` never import from `src/clients`. `test/layers.test.ts` enforces it.
- Model-visible means logged: anything that reaches the model is an event in the session log first.
- Keep the cached prefix byte-identical (see "Cache rules" in `SPEC.md`). Never edit message 0 mid-session.
- Every `tool_use` gets a `tool_result`, including denied and not-started calls.
- API keys only. Never add Claude.ai OAuth, Cursor login, or any request that impersonates another client.
- Never copy code or prompts from `anthropics/claude-code` (no license) or leaked sources, and never port cedia-rs. Adapted Apache-2.0/MIT code needs a `NOTICE` entry.
- e2e tests use the faux provider and must work offline.

## Research

- `research/NOTES.md`: distilled findings with source paths.
- `research/mirror-docs.sh`: re-downloads official docs into `research/docs/` (gitignored). Grep there before searching the web.

# AGENTS.md

Guidance for coding agents working in this repository. `CLAUDE.md` points here.

## What this is

cedia is a personal coding harness written from scratch in TypeScript on Bun. `SPEC.md` holds every settled decision and the stage order; read it before changing scope. `docs/ROADMAP.md` says what comes next.

## Commands

- `bun test`: all tests. One file: `bun test test/layers.test.ts`. One test: add `-t "<name>"`.
- `bun run typecheck`: `tsc --noEmit`.
- `bin/cedia -p "<prompt>" [-m <model>] [--output-format text|json|stream-json] [--permission read-only|workspace] [--allow <rule>] [--deny <rule>]`: headless run. Read-only unless `--permission workspace`. `--check <cmd>` declares a check for the done gate. `--sandbox auto|on|off` controls the OS sandbox for bash (Linux needs bubblewrap, socat, ripgrep). `--fallback <ref|none>` names the model a run continues on when its quota runs out (default `deepseek` → `anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5`). `--plan <ref>` and `--review <ref>` add the plan and review roles (`claude-code[:<model>]` runs them in the user's own Claude Code); `roles` in `~/.cedia/settings.json` sets all three. `CEDIA_CLAUDE_BIN` points tests at a fake `claude`. Every run is a thread of the project: `--thread <id>` goes on with one, `--handoff-at <n|off>` sets when a long session hands off to a new one, `--spawn on|off` and `--swarm <ref>` control sub-threads.
- `bin/cedia threads [list [--all] | show <id> | send <id> <text> | archive <id>]`: the project's threads.
- `bin/cedia lint-session <file.jsonl>...`: check a session log against the trust invariants. `-m faux` with `CEDIA_FAUX_SCRIPT=<steps.json>` runs offline.
- `bun scripts/protocol-schema.ts` regenerates `src/protocol/protocol.schema.json` after a protocol type changes; `bun scripts/session-fixtures.ts` re-records `test/fixtures/sessions/` after the output of a run changes. `test/fixtures.test.ts` fails when either is stale.
- `bun scripts/cache-probe.ts --model <ref> [--turns 20] [--runs 3]`: measure prompt-cache hits on a real model and name every miss.
- `bun evals/run.ts --harness <name> [--model <ref>] [--runs 3] [--jobs 4] [--budget <usd>] [--only <ids>] [--cedia-arg=<flag>]`: run the eval tasks against a harness; `--estimate --model <ref> [--measured <results.jsonl>]` prices a run first. Binaries come from `CEDIA_EVAL_<NAME>_BIN` or PATH. Results go in `evals/results/`.
- `bun evals/gate.ts [--model <ref>] [--estimate] [--update-baseline]`: the regression gate. Runs `evals/gate/suite.json`, prints the expected cost first, compares with `evals/gate/baseline/` and exits 1 when a model got worse. `--compare <results.jsonl>` re-scores a result file for free. Run it before merging a change to a prompt, default, the loop, a tool or the trust layer (`evals/gate/README.md`).

## How to work

Work the pstack poteto-mode way:

- Name the data shapes before writing logic.
- Prove it works: every done-criterion has a test or a command that reruns.
- Decide by experiment (prototype or eval) instead of asking when the question can be measured.
- Small commits, each one a unit that can be checked.

## Rules that are easy to get wrong

- `src/core` and `src/protocol` never import from `src/clients`. `test/layers.test.ts` enforces it.
- Model-visible means logged: anything that reaches the model is an event in the session log first.
- Keep the cached prefix byte-identical (see "Cache rules" in `SPEC.md`). Never edit message 0 mid-session.
- Every `tool_use` gets a `tool_result`, including denied and not-started calls.
- API keys only. Never add Claude.ai OAuth, Cursor login, or any request that impersonates another client.
- Never copy code or prompts from `anthropics/claude-code` (no license) or leaked sources, and never port cedia-rs. Adapted Apache-2.0/MIT code needs a `NOTICE` entry.
- e2e tests use the faux provider and must work offline.

## Research

- `research/NOTES.md`: distilled findings with source paths.
- `research/mirror-docs.sh`: re-downloads official docs into `research/docs/` (gitignored). Grep there before searching the web.

<change>
Three independent changes to the loop and the headless client. Each has its own tests.

1. Loop: malformed turns end or recover instead of misreporting

A reply with only thinking (or nothing) gets one reminder, then fails the run, instead of letting an earlier turn's text stand as the result. A refusal fails the run. A tool that returns no output or an object for text still gets a string result, and a non-Error throw is named. Calls that share an id run once and get one result, so the log stays paired. An unknown tool's name is cut to 64 characters in its result. Cut-off calls alternating with cut-off replies still stop at the turn limit.

2. Go on in a new session when the provider refuses a session's history

A bad_request or context_length error after the session's first accepted request means the history itself is refused (a thinking signature, a tool call the API cannot read back, a context past the window), and resending fails the same way: a left-alone run stopped there, and --thread resumed into the same refused session. The run now goes on once in a new session on the same model, as quota fallback does (parentSession, inherited changes for the done gate, recall, a logged note), and a resumed thread whose last session was refused starts a new one. The thread records it as why: 'rejected'; regenerate the protocol schema (bun scripts/protocol-schema.ts).

3. Wait for a spent quota when asked, up to a ceiling

--on-quota wait:<minutes> (or onQuota in user settings) waits in the same session for a quota error that says when it comes back (a 429 with retry-after), up to that many minutes across the whole run, and falls back only past it. A spent balance names no time and still falls back at once. The default stays fallback. Each wait is a logged attempt, a stderr line, and ends on SIGTERM.
</change>

## Pricing rules

1. A line's subtotal is unit price times quantity.
2. Bulk discount: a line with **10 or more** units gets 5% off that line; **50 or more** units gets 10% off. Only the highest tier applies. Units count per SKU across the whole cart: lines of the same SKU are merged into one before pricing.

6. The total is discounted subtotal + shipping + tax.

import type { Cart } from '../cart/cart.ts';
import { sum, type Cents } from '../money/cents.ts';
import { couponDiscount } from '../pricing/discounts/coupons.ts';
import { priceLine, type PricedLine } from '../pricing/lines.ts';
import { region } from '../pricing/regions.ts';
import { shippingFor } from '../pricing/shipping.ts';
import { taxFor } from '../pricing/tax.ts';

export type Totals = { lines: PricedLine[]; subtotal: Cents; coupon: Cents; shipping: Cents; tax: Cents; total: Cents };

export function totals(c: Cart): Totals {
  const r = region(c.region);
  const lines = c.lines.map(priceLine);
  const subtotal = sum(lines.map((l) => l.total));
  const coupon = couponDiscount(c.coupon, subtotal);
  const discounted = subtotal - coupon;
  const shipping = shippingFor(r, subtotal);
  const tax = taxFor(r, discounted + shipping);
  return { lines, subtotal, coupon, shipping, tax, total: discounted + shipping + tax };
}

import type { Line } from '../cart/cart.ts';
import type { Cents } from '../money/cents.ts';
import { bulkDiscount } from './discounts/bulk.ts';

export type PricedLine = Line & { subtotal: Cents; discount: Cents; total: Cents };

export function priceLine(line: Line): PricedLine {
  const subtotal = line.unitPrice * line.quantity;
  const discount = bulkDiscount(line.quantity, subtotal);
  return { ...line, subtotal, discount, total: subtotal - discount };
}

export type Region = { code: string; taxRate: number; shipping: Cents; freeShippingFrom: Cents };

export const REGIONS: Record<string, Region> = {
  US: { code: 'US', taxRate: 0.07, shipping: 800, freeShippingFrom: 5000 },

  UK: { code: 'UK', taxRate: 0.2, shipping: 700, freeShippingFrom: 4500 },
};

export function region(code: string): Region {
  const r = REGIONS[code];
  if (!r) throw new Error(`unknown region ${code}`);
  return r;
}

import type { Cents } from '../money/cents.ts';
import type { Region } from './regions.ts';

// What shipping costs for an order whose amount, as the caller decides it, is `amount`.
export function shippingFor(r: Region, amount: Cents): Cents {
  return amount >= r.freeShippingFrom ? 0 : r.shipping;
}

// Tiers from the highest down; the first that applies wins.
const TIERS = [

import type { Cents } from '../../money/cents.ts';
import { percentOf } from '../../money/round.ts';

export type Coupon = { code: string; apply(amount: Cents): Cents };

const COUPONS: Coupon[] = [
  { code: 'SAVE10', apply: (amount) => percentOf(amount, 0.1) },
  { code: 'FLAT5', apply: (amount) => Math.min(500, amount) },
];

// The discount a coupon gives on an amount; unknown codes give none.
export function couponDiscount(code: string | undefined, amount: Cents): Cents {
  if (!code) return 0;
  const c = COUPONS.find((x) => x.code === code.toUpperCase());
  return c ? c.apply(amount) : 0;
}

import type { Cents } from './cents.ts';

// Half up: 12.5 -> 13. Tax amounts are never negative, so the sign rule does not matter here.
export function roundHalfUp(x: number): Cents {
  return Math.floor(x + 0.5);
}

// Applies a rate (0.2 for 20%) to an amount and rounds once.
export function percentOf(amount: Cents, rate: number): Cents {
  return roundHalfUp(amount * rate);
}

import type { Cart } from './cart.ts';

// Two lines of the same sku become one; the cart keeps the first coupon it saw.
export function mergeLines(c: Cart): Cart {
  const by = new Map<string, Cart['lines'][number]>();
  for (const l of c.lines) {
    const seen = by.get(l.sku);
    if (seen) seen.quantity += l.quantity;
    else by.set(l.sku, { ...l });
  }
  return { ...c, lines: [...by.values()] };
}

## Pricing rules

1. A line's subtotal is unit price times quantity.
2. Bulk discount: a line with **10 or more** units gets 5% off that line; **50 or more** units gets 10% off. Only the highest tier applies. Units count per SKU across the whole cart: lines of the same SKU are merged into one before pricing.
3. Coupons apply to the order after bulk discounts: `SAVE10` takes 10% off, `FLAT5` takes 500 cents off (never below zero). One coupon per order.
4. Shipping: each region has a flat rate and a free-shipping threshold. Shipping is free when the **discounted** subtotal (after bulk discounts and the coupon, before tax) is at least the threshold.
5. Tax is charged on the discounted subtotal plus shipping, at the region's rate, rounded half up to the cent.
6. The total is discounted subtotal + shipping + tax.

export type PricedLine = Line & { subtotal: Cents; discount: Cents; total: Cents };

export function priceLine(line: Line): PricedLine {
  const subtotal = line.unitPrice * line.quantity;
  const discount = bulkDiscount(line.quantity, subtotal);
  return { ...line, subtotal, discount, total: subtotal - discount };

import type { Cents } from '../../money/cents.ts';
import { percentOf } from '../../money/round.ts';

// Tiers from the highest down; the first that applies wins.
const TIERS = [
  { min: 50, rate: 0.1 },
  { min: 10, rate: 0.05 },
];

export function bulkDiscount(quantity: number, subtotal: Cents): Cents {
  const tier = TIERS.find((t) => quantity > t.min);
  return tier ? percentOf(subtotal, tier.rate) : 0;
}

import type { Cents } from '../../money/cents.ts';
import { percentOf } from '../../money/round.ts';

export type Coupon = { code: string; apply(amount: Cents): Cents };

const COUPONS: Coupon[] = [
  { code: 'SAVE10', apply: (amount) => percentOf(amount, 0.1) },
  { code: 'FLAT5', apply: (amount) => Math.min(500, amount) },
];

// The discount a coupon gives on an amount; unknown codes give none.
export function couponDiscount(code: string | undefined, amount: Cents): Cents {
  if (!code) return 0;
  const c = COUPONS.find((x) => x.code === code.toUpperCase());
  return c ? c.apply(amount) : 0;
}

// Whole cents. Fractions only appear inside a calculation and are rounded once, at the end of it.
export type Cents = number;

export const cents = (n: number): Cents => Math.round(n);

export function sum(values: Cents[]): Cents {
  return values.reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0);
}

import type { Cents } from './cents.ts';

// Half up: 12.5 -> 13. Tax amounts are never negative, so the sign rule does not matter here.
export function roundHalfUp(x: number): Cents {
  return Math.floor(x + 0.5);
}

// Applies a rate (0.2 for 20%) to an amount and rounds once.
export function percentOf(amount: Cents, rate: number): Cents {
  return roundHalfUp(amount * rate);
}

export function totals(c: Cart): Totals {
  const r = region(c.region);
  const lines = c.lines.map(priceLine);
  const subtotal = sum(lines.map((l) => l.total));
  const coupon = couponDiscount(c.coupon, subtotal);
  const discounted = subtotal - coupon;
  const shipping = shippingFor(r, subtotal);
  const tax = taxFor(r, discounted + shipping);
  return { lines, subtotal, coupon, shipping, tax, total: discounted + shipping + tax };
}

import type { Cart } from './cart.ts';

// Two lines of the same sku become one; the cart keeps the first coupon it saw.
export function mergeLines(c: Cart): Cart {
  const by = new Map<string, Cart['lines'][number]>();
  for (const l of c.lines) {
    const seen = by.get(l.sku);
    if (seen) seen.quantity += l.quantity;
    else by.set(l.sku, { ...l });
  }
  return { ...c, lines: [...by.values()] };
}

//
// slugify(text, max?):
// - lower case;
// - a letter with an accent or other diacritic loses it (à -> a, ç -> c, ñ -> n, ź -> z, and so on);
//   ß -> ss, æ -> ae, œ -> oe, ø -> o, ł -> l, đ -> d;

// - with max, a slug longer than max is cut at the last "-" that keeps it within max (no dangling "-"), or at
//   max itself when there is no "-" to cut at. A "-" right after the first max characters counts: cutting there
//   keeps exactly max ("ab-cd-ef" with max 5 is "ab-cd").
//
// uniqueSlug(slug, taken): slug itself if it is not in taken, else slug-2, slug-3, ... the first free one.
const SPECIAL: Record<string, string> = { ß: 'ss', æ: 'ae', œ: 'oe', ø: 'o', ł: 'l', đ: 'd' };

export function slugify(text: string, max?: number): string {
  const base = text
    .toLowerCase()
    .replace(/[ßæœøłđ]/g, (c) => SPECIAL[c])
    .normalize('NFD')
    .replace(/\p{M}/gu, '')
    .replace(/[^a-z0-9]+/g, '-')
    .replace(/^-+|-+$/g, '');
  if (max === undefined || base.length <= max) return base;
  if (base[max] === '-') return base.slice(0, max);
  const cut = base.lastIndexOf('-', max);
  return cut > 0 ? base.slice(0, cut) : base.slice(0, max);
}

export function uniqueSlug(slug: string, taken: Set<string>): string {
  if (!taken.has(slug)) return slug;
  let n = 2;
  while (taken.has(`${slug}-${n}`)) n++;
  return `${slug}-${n}`;
}

// A least-recently-used cache whose entries also expire.
//
// new LRU(capacity, ttlMs, now = Date.now):
// - get(key): the value, or undefined when missing or expired. A hit makes the entry the most recently used.
//   An expired entry is removed when it is found, with onEvict(key, value, 'expired').
// - set(key, value): stores it as the most recently used, with a fresh ttl. When that takes the cache over
//   capacity, the least recently used entry is removed with onEvict(key, value, 'capacity'). Capacity counts
//   every stored entry, expired or not. Expired entries are removed first (reason 'expired'), and only if the
//   cache is still over capacity is a live one evicted.
// - delete(key): true if a live entry was removed (onEvict reason 'delete'); an expired one is removed with
//   reason 'expired' and delete returns false.
// - size: the number of live (unexpired) entries.
// - keys(): live keys, most recently used first.
// An entry set at time t expires at t + ttlMs: it is live while now() < t + ttlMs.
export type EvictReason = 'capacity' | 'expired' | 'delete';

interface Entry<V> {
  value: V;
  expiresAt: number;
}

export class LRU<K, V> {
  onEvict?: (key: K, value: V, reason: EvictReason) => void;
  // Map keeps insertion order: first entry is least recently used.
  private entries = new Map<K, Entry<V>>();

  constructor(
    private capacity: number,
    private ttlMs: number,
    private now: () => number = Date.now,
  ) {}

  private isLive(entry: Entry<V>): boolean {
    return this.now() < entry.expiresAt;
  }

  get(key: K): V | undefined {
    const entry = this.entries.get(key);
    if (entry === undefined) return undefined;
    this.entries.delete(key);
    if (!this.isLive(entry)) {
      this.onEvict?.(key, entry.value, 'expired');
      return undefined;
    }
    this.entries.set(key, entry);
    return entry.value;
  }

  set(key: K, value: V): void {
    this.entries.delete(key);
    this.entries.set(key, { value, expiresAt: this.now() + this.ttlMs });
    if (this.entries.size <= this.capacity) return;
    for (const [k, e] of [...this.entries]) {
      if (!this.isLive(e)) {
        this.entries.delete(k);
        this.onEvict?.(k, e.value, 'expired');
      }
    }
    while (this.entries.size > this.capacity) {
      const [k, e] = this.entries.entries().next().value!;
      this.entries.delete(k);
      this.onEvict?.(k, e.value, 'capacity');
    }
  }

  delete(key: K): boolean {
    const entry = this.entries.get(key);
    if (entry === undefined) return false;
    this.entries.delete(key);
    if (!this.isLive(entry)) {
      this.onEvict?.(key, entry.value, 'expired');
      return false;
    }
    this.onEvict?.(key, entry.value, 'delete');
    return true;
  }

  get size(): number {
    let n = 0;
    for (const e of this.entries.values()) if (this.isLive(e)) n++;
    return n;
  }

  keys(): K[] {
    const out: K[] = [];
    for (const [k, e] of this.entries) if (this.isLive(e)) out.push(k);
    return out.reverse();
  }
}

// Durations as text, for config files and logs.
//
// parseDuration: one or more <number><unit> parts, optionally separated by spaces: "90s", "1h30m", "1.5h",
// "2d 4h", "250ms". Spaces around the whole text are ignored. Units: d, h, m, s, ms. Numbers may have a
// fraction. Returns milliseconds, rounded to a whole number. Throws an Error whose message contains the input
// for anything else: "", "10", "5x", "h", "-1s".
//
// formatDuration: milliseconds to the shortest text using d, h, m, s and ms, largest unit first, zero parts
// left out, no spaces: 5_400_000 -> "1h30m", 1_500 -> "1s500ms", 0 -> "0s". Throws on a negative number.
const UNIT_MS: Record<string, number> = { d: 86_400_000, h: 3_600_000, m: 60_000, s: 1_000, ms: 1 };
const PART = /(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)(ms|d|h|m|s)/g;
const WHOLE = /^(?:\d+(?:\.\d+)?(?:ms|d|h|m|s)\s*)*\d+(?:\.\d+)?(?:ms|d|h|m|s)$/;

export function parseDuration(text: string): number {
  const input = text.trim();
  if (!WHOLE.test(input)) throw new Error(`invalid duration: "${text}"`);
  let total = 0;
  for (const [, amount, unit] of input.matchAll(PART)) {
    total += Number(amount) * UNIT_MS[unit];
  }
  return Math.round(total);
}

export function formatDuration(ms: number): string {
  if (ms < 0) throw new Error(`negative duration: ${ms}`);
  let rest = Math.round(ms);
  if (rest === 0) return '0s';
  let out = '';
  for (const unit of ['d', 'h', 'm', 's', 'ms'] as const) {
    const n = Math.floor(rest / UNIT_MS[unit]);
    if (n > 0) out += `${n}${unit}`;
    rest -= n * UNIT_MS[unit];
  }
  return out;
}

// URL slugs for titles.
//
// slugify(text, max?):
// - lower case;
// - a letter with an accent or other diacritic loses it (à -> a, ç -> c, ñ -> n, ź -> z, and so on);
//   ß -> ss, æ -> ae, œ -> oe, ø -> o, ł -> l, đ -> d;
// - any other character that is not a-z or 0-9 is a separator; runs of separators become one "-", and the slug
//   never starts or ends with "-";
// - with max, a slug longer than max is cut at the last "-" that keeps it within max (no dangling "-"), or at
//   max itself when there is no "-" to cut at. A "-" right after the first max characters counts: cutting there
//   keeps exactly max ("ab-cd-ef" with max 5 is "ab-cd").
//
// uniqueSlug(slug, taken): slug itself if it is not in taken, else slug-2, slug-3, ... the first free one.
const SPECIAL: Record<string, string> = { ß: 'ss', æ: 'ae', œ: 'oe', ø: 'o', ł: 'l', đ: 'd' };

export function slugify(text: string, max?: number): string {
  const base = text
    .toLowerCase()
    .replace(/[ßæœøłđ]/g, (c) => SPECIAL[c])
    .normalize('NFD')
    .replace(/\p{M}/gu, '')
    .replace(/[^a-z0-9]+/g, '-')
    .replace(/^-+|-+$/g, '');
  if (max === undefined || base.length <= max) return base;
  if (base[max] === '-') return base.slice(0, max);
  const cut = base.lastIndexOf('-', max);
  return cut > 0 ? base.slice(0, cut) : base.slice(0, max);
}

export function uniqueSlug(slug: string, taken: Set<string>): string {
  if (!taken.has(slug)) return slug;
  let n = 2;
  while (taken.has(`${slug}-${n}`)) n++;
  return `${slug}-${n}`;
}

// A least-recently-used cache whose entries also expire.
//
// new LRU(capacity, ttlMs, now = Date.now):
// - get(key): the value, or undefined when missing or expired. A hit makes the entry the most recently used.
//   An expired entry is removed when it is found, with onEvict(key, value, 'expired').
// - set(key, value): stores it as the most recently used, with a fresh ttl. When that takes the cache over
//   capacity, the least recently used entry is removed with onEvict(key, value, 'capacity'). Capacity counts
//   every stored entry, expired or not. Expired entries are removed first (reason 'expired'), and only if the
//   cache is still over capacity is a live one evicted.
// - delete(key): true if a live entry was removed (onEvict reason 'delete'); an expired one is removed with
//   reason 'expired' and delete returns false.
// - size: the number of live (unexpired) entries.
// - keys(): live keys, most recently used first.
// An entry set at time t expires at t + ttlMs: it is live while now() < t + ttlMs.
export type EvictReason = 'capacity' | 'expired' | 'delete';

interface Entry<V> {
  value: V;
  expiresAt: number;
}

export class LRU<K, V> {
  onEvict?: (key: K, value: V, reason: EvictReason) => void;
  // Map keeps insertion order: first entry is least recently used.
  private entries = new Map<K, Entry<V>>();

  constructor(
    private capacity: number,
    private ttlMs: number,
    private now: () => number = Date.now,
  ) {}

  private isLive(entry: Entry<V>): boolean {
    return this.now() < entry.expiresAt;
  }

  get(key: K): V | undefined {
    const entry = this.entries.get(key);
    if (entry === undefined) return undefined;
    this.entries.delete(key);
    if (!this.isLive(entry)) {
      this.onEvict?.(key, entry.value, 'expired');
      return undefined;
    }
    this.entries.set(key, entry);
    return entry.value;
  }

  set(key: K, value: V): void {
    this.entries.delete(key);
    this.entries.set(key, { value, expiresAt: this.now() + this.ttlMs });
    if (this.entries.size <= this.capacity) return;
    for (const [k, e] of [...this.entries]) {
      if (!this.isLive(e)) {
        this.entries.delete(k);
        this.onEvict?.(k, e.value, 'expired');
      }
    }
    while (this.entries.size > this.capacity) {
      const [k, e] = this.entries.entries().next().value!;
      this.entries.delete(k);
      this.onEvict?.(k, e.value, 'capacity');
    }
  }

  delete(key: K): boolean {
    const entry = this.entries.get(key);
    if (entry === undefined) return false;
    this.entries.delete(key);
    if (!this.isLive(entry)) {
      this.onEvict?.(key, entry.value, 'expired');
      return false;
    }
    this.onEvict?.(key, entry.value, 'delete');
    return true;
  }

  get size(): number {
    let n = 0;
    for (const e of this.entries.values()) if (this.isLive(e)) n++;
    return n;
  }

  keys(): K[] {
    const out: K[] = [];
    for (const [k, e] of this.entries) if (this.isLive(e)) out.push(k);
    return out.reverse();
  }
}

import { expect, test } from 'bun:test';
import { formatDuration, parseDuration } from '../src/duration.ts';
import { slugify, uniqueSlug } from '../src/slug.ts';
import { LRU } from '../src/lru.ts';

test('parseDuration rules', () => {
  expect(parseDuration(' 2d 4h ')).toBe(187_200_000);
  expect(parseDuration('250ms')).toBe(250);
  expect(parseDuration('1.5h')).toBe(5_400_000);
  expect(parseDuration('1s500ms')).toBe(1_500);
  for (const bad of ['', '10', '5x', 'h', '-1s']) {
    expect(() => parseDuration(bad)).toThrow(bad);
  }
});

test('formatDuration rules', () => {
  expect(formatDuration(1_500)).toBe('1s500ms');
  expect(formatDuration(0)).toBe('0s');
  expect(formatDuration(90_000_000)).toBe('1d1h');
  expect(() => formatDuration(-1)).toThrow();
});

test('slugify rules', () => {
  expect(slugify('Straße Æble Øl Łódź Đ')).toBe('strasse-aeble-ol-lodz-d');
  expect(slugify('ab-cd-ef', 5)).toBe('ab-cd');
  expect(slugify('abcdefgh-ij', 5)).toBe('abcde');
  expect(slugify('  --Hi!!  ')).toBe('hi');
});

test('uniqueSlug rules', () => {
  expect(uniqueSlug('post', new Set())).toBe('post');
  expect(uniqueSlug('post', new Set(['post', 'post-2']))).toBe('post-3');
});

test('LRU rules', () => {
  let t = 0;
  const evicted: string[] = [];
  const cache = new LRU<string, number>(2, 100, () => t);
  cache.onEvict = (k, _v, r) => evicted.push(`${k}:${r}`);
  cache.set('a', 1);
  cache.set('b', 2);
  expect(cache.get('a')).toBe(1);
  cache.set('c', 3);
  expect(evicted).toEqual(['b:capacity']);
  t = 99;
  expect(cache.size).toBe(2);
  t = 100;
  expect(cache.size).toBe(0);
  expect(cache.keys()).toEqual([]);
  expect(cache.delete('a')).toBe(false);
  expect(evicted).toEqual(['b:capacity', 'a:expired', 'c:expired']);
});

test('LRU delete and expired-first eviction', () => {
  let t = 0;
  const evicted: string[] = [];
  const cache = new LRU<string, number>(2, 10, () => t);
  cache.onEvict = (k, _v, r) => evicted.push(`${k}:${r}`);
  cache.set('a', 1);
  t = 5;
  cache.set('b', 2);
  expect(cache.delete('b')).toBe(true);
  t = 10;
  cache.set('c', 3);
  cache.set('d', 4);
  expect(evicted).toEqual(['b:delete', 'a:expired']);
  expect(cache.keys()).toEqual(['d', 'c']);
});

// parseDuration: one or more <number><unit> parts, optionally separated by spaces: "90s", "1h30m", "1.5h",

// left out, no spaces: 5_400_000 -> "1h30m", 1_500 -> "1s500ms", 0 -> "0s". Throws on a negative number.
const UNITS: [string, number][] = [
  ['d', 86_400_000],
  ['h', 3_600_000],
  ['m', 60_000],
  ['s', 1_000],
  ['ms', 1],
];

const PART = /(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)(ms|d|h|m|s)\s*/y;

export function parseDuration(text: string): number {
  const input = text.trim();
  if (input === '') throw new Error(`invalid duration: "${text}"`);
  let total = 0;
  let pos = 0;
  while (pos < input.length) {
    PART.lastIndex = pos;
    const match = PART.exec(input);
    if (!match) throw new Error(`invalid duration: "${text}"`);
    const unit = UNITS.find(([name]) => name === match[2])!;
    total += Number(match[1]) * unit[1];
    pos = PART.lastIndex;
  }
  return Math.round(total);
}

export function formatDuration(ms: number): string {
  if (ms < 0) throw new Error(`negative duration: ${ms}`);
  let rest = Math.round(ms);
  let out = '';
  for (const [name, size] of UNITS) {
    const n = Math.floor(rest / size);
    if (n > 0) out += `${n}${name}`;
    rest -= n * size;
  }
  return out || '0s';
}

// URL slugs for titles.
//
// slugify(text, max?):
// - lower case;
// - a letter with an accent or other diacritic loses it (à -> a, ç -> c, ñ -> n, ź -> z, and so on);
//   ß -> ss, æ -> ae, œ -> oe, ø -> o, ł -> l, đ -> d;
// - any other character that is not a-z or 0-9 is a separator; runs of separators become one "-", and the slug
//   never starts or ends with "-";
// - with max, a slug longer than max is cut at the last "-" that keeps it within max (no dangling "-"), or at
//   max itself when there is no "-" to cut at. A "-" right after the first max characters counts: cutting there
//   keeps exactly max ("ab-cd-ef" with max 5 is "ab-cd").
//
// uniqueSlug(slug, taken): slug itself if it is not in taken, else slug-2, slug-3, ... the first free one.
const SPECIAL: Record<string, string> = {
  ß: 'ss',
  æ: 'ae',
  œ: 'oe',
  ø: 'o',
  ł: 'l',
  đ: 'd',
};

export function slugify(text: string, max?: number): string {
  const slug = text
    .toLowerCase()
    .replace(/[ßæœøłđ]/g, (c) => SPECIAL[c])
    .normalize('NFD')
    .replace(/\p{M}/gu, '')
    .replace(/[^a-z0-9]+/g, '-')
    .replace(/^-|-$/g, '');
  if (max === undefined || slug.length <= max) return slug;
  const cut = slug[max] === '-' ? max : slug.lastIndexOf('-', max - 1);
  return slug.slice(0, cut === -1 ? max : cut);
}

export function uniqueSlug(slug: string, taken: Set<string>): string {
  if (!taken.has(slug)) return slug;
  let n = 2;
  while (taken.has(`${slug}-${n}`)) n++;
  return `${slug}-${n}`;
}

// A least-recently-used cache whose entries also expire.
//
// new LRU(capacity, ttlMs, now = Date.now):
// - get(key): the value, or undefined when missing or expired. A hit makes the entry the most recently used.
//   An expired entry is removed when it is found, with onEvict(key, value, 'expired').
// - set(key, value): stores it as the most recently used, with a fresh ttl. When that takes the cache over
//   capacity, the least recently used entry is removed with onEvict(key, value, 'capacity'). Capacity counts
//   every stored entry, expired or not. Expired entries are removed first (reason 'expired'), and only if the
//   cache is still over capacity is a live one evicted.
// - delete(key): true if a live entry was removed (onEvict reason 'delete'); an expired one is removed with
//   reason 'expired' and delete returns false.
// - size: the number of live (unexpired) entries.
// - keys(): live keys, most recently used first.
// An entry set at time t expires at t + ttlMs: it is live while now() < t + ttlMs.
export type EvictReason = 'capacity' | 'expired' | 'delete';

interface Entry<V> {
  value: V;
  expires: number;
}

export class LRU<K, V> {
  onEvict?: (key: K, value: V, reason: EvictReason) => void;

  // Map keeps insertion order, so the first key is the least recently used.
  private entries = new Map<K, Entry<V>>();

  constructor(
    private capacity: number,
    private ttlMs: number,
    private now: () => number = Date.now,
  ) {}

  private isExpired(entry: Entry<V>): boolean {
    return this.now() >= entry.expires;
  }

  get(key: K): V | undefined {
    const entry = this.entries.get(key);
    if (!entry) return undefined;
    this.entries.delete(key);
    if (this.isExpired(entry)) {
      this.onEvict?.(key, entry.value, 'expired');
      return undefined;
    }
    this.entries.set(key, entry);
    return entry.value;
  }

  set(key: K, value: V): void {
    this.entries.delete(key);
    this.entries.set(key, { value, expires: this.now() + this.ttlMs });
    if (this.entries.size <= this.capacity) return;
    for (const [k, entry] of [...this.entries]) {
      if (this.isExpired(entry)) {
        this.entries.delete(k);
        this.onEvict?.(k, entry.value, 'expired');
      }
    }
    while (this.entries.size > this.capacity) {
      const [k, entry] = this.entries.entries().next().value!;
      this.entries.delete(k);
      this.onEvict?.(k, entry.value, 'capacity');
    }
  }

  delete(key: K): boolean {
    const entry = this.entries.get(key);
    if (!entry) return false;
    this.entries.delete(key);
    if (this.isExpired(entry)) {
      this.onEvict?.(key, entry.value, 'expired');
      return false;
    }
    this.onEvict?.(key, entry.value, 'delete');
    return true;
  }

  get size(): number {
    return this.keys().length;
  }

  keys(): K[] {
    const live: K[] = [];
    for (const [k, entry] of this.entries) {
      if (!this.isExpired(entry)) live.push(k);
    }
    return live.reverse();
  }
}
